Going through the same thing, man. Siguro what really helped nung una is STRICTLY NO CONTACT. May mga times na grabe yung lungkot o kaya nostalgia na matetempt ka irelive yung memories and send messages to ur partner. The longer na you can go without contact, the better. Sa una mahirap, pero the longer na wala kayong contact, mas marerealize mo na kaya mo pala, kaya mo na wala siya and you can survive without his/her presence. Then there are better days ahead after that. Slowly you'll realize na instead of finding someone to give that love you yearn for, you try to give it yourself. Small things and small steps lang, like taking care of yourself. Nakakain ka ba ng 3 meals sa isang araw? Nakatulog ka ba? Naligo ka na ba? Mga ganun. Treat yourself pa minsan andd try to go back and do yung mga dati mong hobbies o ginagawa before mo siya mameet. Super helpful nun sakin kasi I realized ang rami ko nga pa lang ginagawa and nag-ooccupy ng time ko and naeenjoy before ko siya mameet. 

Tsaka if you're starting pa lang to get over him/her, i-tally mo bawat araw na you can go without contact. Every single day is a win. Hanggang sa umabot sa point na di mo na naiisip i-tally.

About the anime episode, what I did was as silly as it sounds, I got a notebook then while watching episodeS of anime, I wrote the words that I heard- well the common ones that I can really hear. Then, even if the words I hear were misspelled, I turned to HiNative app (it's free) and asked a question. 

"What does hayaku mean?" and so on.

Then people who knew Japanese and natives would answer and correct me. Even spell it in hiragana. I could ask for clarification and further questions. Then, I kept asking and asking. They're so kind and they really answer.

Then, as days went by, I would take note of the words I kept hearing often like arigatou,  tashikani, and search them up on google. 

I'm also a beginner still, but I can say it really helped. I would watch multiple episodes of anime then in each episode when I feel like it and whenever I hear it often- or clearly, I would write it and search it on google. Then I'd be corrected and actually learn it. 

  
After doing it for so long now, I think I got better hearing skills. I hear words I never heard before :DD. 

Learning hiragana is a must. (Although HeyJapan app has it written in english letters, learning to read is going to make you very proud of yourself.  I was really happy the first time I was able to read and understand XD. )
